problem:
Find a $2\times 2$ matrix $F$ that has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-2,$ and corresponding eigenvectors

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$

feedback.problem:
Find a $2\times 2$ matrix $E$ that has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-5,$ and corresponding eigenvectors

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $B={{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}$ is a basis of ${R}^{2}$ consisting of the eigenvectors of $E,$ then $E$ must be diagonalizable.

So, we can write $E=PD{P}^{-1},$ where $P$ is a matrix whose columns are the eigenvectors of $E,$ and $D$ is a diagonal matrix whose entries are the eigenvalues in the corresponding order:

$$
E={{[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {v}_{1} & {v}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda }_{2}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{{[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {v}_{1} & {v}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

Let $P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}].$ Then,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{-1} & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, carrying out the necessary matrix multiplication, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}E & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & -5\end{aligned}](\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}9 & -15 \\ 12 & -30\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 & -3 \\ -4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}19 & -12 \\ 32 & -21\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
